subject: Allocation ladder & preempt policy proposal for dedicated capacity - Auriga
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@auriga.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aaron Cole <aaron.c@auriga.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated start & potential contention with other deals

Hi Soojin —

Thanks again for the intro call yesterday. As we finalize commercial terms for our Dedicated capacity (target go-live: 2028-10-01), we want to surface one concern: our internal models need sustained low-latency access to ~8 A100-equivalent GPUs for serving during business hours (14:00–22:00 UTC). We heard there are other Q4 commitments in the same cluster region and wanted to understand Redwood's policy if capacity contention arises.

Specifically:
- Will our reserved tranche be preemptible if higher-priority enterprise deals come online?
- Are there staged fallback options (smaller model variants, quantized replicas) that Redwood recommends automatically?
- What escalation path should we expect if we see perf degradation?

We need clarity to finalize our infra spend and feature gating plan. Happy to hop on a quick call with your infra team.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Head of ML Ops
Auriga AI

P.S. Aaron attached a rough forecast (we'll upload the spreadsheet to your portal).

Hi Maya —

Appreciate the heads-up and very reasonable questions. Short answer: for committed Dedicated capacity we aim to provide predictable throughput and minimize preemption, but there are edge cases during fleet stress where we rely on a prioritization policy.

Looping in Vivek (Infra) and Monica (Customer Success) so we can propose a concrete allocation ladder and fallback plan that matches your SLA needs. Rishi, FYI on the ask — this is on the critical path for closing the signature.

Proposed next steps:
1) Vivek to share the recommended "allocation ladder" and preemption windows (technical constraints + mitigation).
2) Monica to outline customer-facing commitments we can reasonably document in the SOW (non-preemptible tranche vs. burst lanes).
3) Schedule 30m call (this week) to review and lock terms.

Would Thursday 2028-09-07 at 10:00 PT work for you?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Maya Singh <maya@auriga.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 Sep 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Allocation ladder proposal + suggested preempt policy

Hi all —

Thanks for flagging this. Below is a pragmatic allocation ladder we've used in other deals; it balances predictability for committed customers and operational flexibility during capacity stress. I'm attaching a one-page PDF and a Q4 capacity workbook with current reservations.

Allocation ladder (highest -> lowest):
1) Reserved non-preemptible (Enterprise-SLA): hard guarantee, slices pinned to tranche; requires commercial commit (min 6 months).
2) Reserved preemptible (Committed): commitments with defined soft-preemption windows (we allow reclaiming during off-peak only with 30m notice).
3) Burst pool: short-lived reserved capacity for transient spikes; limited per-customer burst budget.
4) Opportunistic / Spot: lowest-cost, no SLA — reclaimed immediately under pressure.

Preemption policy (operational highlights):
- Preemption events are staged during low-util windows where possible (we avoid business-hours preemption for Reserved Non-preemptible).
- We provide automated model-fallback hooks: customers can register prioritized fallback variants (e.g., 8xA100 -> 4xGPU quantized) to gracefully degrade latency/cost.
- Grace period: when preemption is triggered, affected instances receive a 10-minute soft-drain signal (streaming responses continue; new sessions redirected).
- Rolling migration: we prefer rolling scale-down over immediate kill to reduce 429s/connection resets.

Constraints and notes:
- Q4 fleet commitments already include two large Reserved deals (enterprise) scheduled 2028-10—2028-12. If Auriga chooses non-preemptible Reserved, we can honor it, but it requires booking by 2028-09-14 to lock tranche placement in the regional pool.
- If booked late, we can offer a hybrid: partial non-preemptible slice + burstable pool.

I'll highlight tradeoffs during Thursday's call. Attaching: allocation_ladder_v1.pdf; q4_capacity_plan.xlsx.

—Vivek
Director, Infrastructure Delivery
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Maya Singh <maya@auriga.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 7 Sep 2028 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Allocation ladder proposal + suggested preempt policy

Hi Maya —

From a CS standpoint, two asks before we finalize contract language:
1) If Auriga needs a full non-preemptible tranche for the first 6 months, we can carve that with a price uplift and a migration window commitment in the SOW. Please confirm desired GPU count and peak windows so we can size the slice.
2) If you opt for a hybrid (partial reserved + burst), we want to define clear observability hooks and an escalation-runbook (pager list + SLA credits triggers) — this prevents surprise during capacity events.

Soojin/Rishi: if we commit the 6-month non-preemptible tranche, legal and finance will need a side letter with the uplift and termination notice (60 days). Let's capture in the MAP.

Maya: can you confirm: final ask is 8 A100-equivalent GPUs w/ primary traffic window 14:00–22:00 UTC Tues–Fri (as discussed)? If yes, we'll prepare an SOW draft for review.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@auriga.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 7 Sep 2028 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Allocation ladder proposal + suggested preempt policy

Maya / Aaron —

Thanks for the quick responses and for confirming details on the call. Summary / mutual action plan (MAP):
- Auriga to confirm final GPU quantity by EOD 2028-09-08 (Auriga provided target: 8 A100-equivalents; please confirm).
- Redwood to hold an allocation ladder placement spot until 2028-09-14 pending signed SOW + initial payment for a 6-month non-preemptible tranche.
- If Auriga signs after 2028-09-14, Redwood will offer a hybrid tranche (4 non-preemptible + burst pool) at the same uplift rate but no tranche placement guarantee.
- Redwood to provide runbook and observability hooks (pager, SLA-credit triggers, fallback registration API) within 3 business days post-signature.
- Next meeting: 30m contract finalization call on Friday 2028-09-08 at 09:00 PT (calendar invite sent).

Attachments referenced: allocation_ladder_v1.pdf, q4_capacity_plan.xlsx.

Please reply-all with any edits to the MAP; if green, we'll convert to the SOW and legal will prepare the side letter for the non-preemptible uplift.

Best,
Soojin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
